sources.source: MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution (Boncz, Zukowski, Nes, CIDR 2005)

items.item: Volcano iterator's tuple-at-a-time pull causes high interpretation overhead and hides CPU parallelism from the compiler

items.item: X100's default vector size is 1024; the optimal size on their workload was about 1000, with 128–8K all working well, degrading once vectors overflow the CPU cache

items.item: DuckDB uses a vectorized query execution model, with a default vector size (STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE) of 2048 tuples

sources.source: Efficiently Compiling Efficient Query Plans for Modern Hardware (Neumann, VLDB 2011, HyPer)

items.item: The classical iterator model is simple and flexible but performs poorly on modern CPUs due to lack of locality and instruction mispredictions

items.item: HyPer's compiled model: processing is data-centric not operator-centric, and data is pushed toward consumers rather than pulled

sources.source: Morsel-Driven Parallelism: A NUMA-Aware Query Evaluation Framework for the Many-Core Age (Leis, Boncz, Kemper, Neumann, SIGMOD 2014)

items.item: Morsels: small fragments of input dispatched to worker threads that run a whole pipeline until the next pipeline breaker, with the degree of parallelism free to change at run time
